newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish lower after U.S. jobs report.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish lower after U.S. jobs report.

text.p: French stocks finished lower on Friday after a robust U.S. jobs report that fanned concerns about the outlook for U.S. interest rates drove down Wall Street stocks.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 21.58 points, or 0.92 percent, at 2,327.50, but ended the week 1.9 percent higher. The CAC-40 futures contract fell 20 points to 2,331 on Friday.
Volume was a heavy eight billion francs.
The poor performance of the Tokyo market, which ended the week at a two-year low after a string of losses, had also unnerved the bourse, but investors said the driving force remains the U.S. market.
They said investors will be waiting to see U.S. consumer inflation data due on Tuesday.
The jobs report showed 262,000 new jobs in December, far above the consensus estimate of 192,000. The U.S. unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.3 percent.
Speculation about restructurings of the French banking and pharmaceutical industries enlivened trading on the bourse.
Shares in Elf-Aquitaine drugs subsidiary Sanofi rallied 6.17 percent to 568 francs on rumours of a deal with Synthelabo, majority-controlled by cosmetics giant L'Oreal.
Synthelabo denied the rumour, while L'Oreal declined comment.
The sector is rife with speculation following a number of mergers, and Sanofi's stock has become closely watched since Elf said recently that it would be willing to give up control.
Via Banque, a subsidiary of Paribas, rallied 8.43 percent to 193 francs on market speculation that it may be the next Paribas asset up for sale.

The financial group said on Thursday that it would sell bank Credit du Nord to Societe Generale. Paribas' stock eased 0.31 percent to 353.10 francs on Friday after gaining 4.02 percent on the previous day.
